name: Royal Hill of Ambohimanga
subtitle: A cultural property on the UNESCO World Heritage List since 2001.

parts.text: UNESCO describes the property in these words: “The Royal Hill of Ambohimanga consists of a royal city and burial site, and an ensemble of sacred places. It is associated with strong feelings of national identity, and has maintained its spiritual and sacred character both in ritual practice and the popular imagination for the past 500 years. It remains a place of worship to which pilgrims come from Madagascar and elsewhere.”

Ambohimanga is a hill and fortified royal settlement, a rova, about 24 kilometres north-east of Antananarivo. Wikipedia calls it the most significant symbol of Merina cultural identity and the best-preserved monument of the precolonial Merina Kingdom.
It is one of the twelve sacred hills of Imerina and a place of worship to which pilgrims still come from Madagascar and elsewhere.

The article says it became politically important in the early 18th century, when King Andriamasinavalona divided Imerina into four quadrants and gave his son the north-east one, ruled from Ambohimanga.

gaps: Malagasy voices on the sacred hill and its rituals, beyond the article's summary.
The Rova of Antananarivo is a different royal site and this card does not cover it.
